prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: visual implementation reference for an actual desktop GUI, not marketing artwork.
Image 1 is the authoritative approved style reference. Extend its exact sophisticated black-blue optical-glass language to NEW components. Maintain opaque ink-navy faces with believable optical thickness, a crisp narrow icy pale-blue inner bevel, fine cyan outer edge, subtle secondary recessed inner contour, layered translucent triangular corner shards that taper and fade smoothly toward a mostly quiet middle, sharp-edged low-contrast reflection planes and occasional small intense white-cyan glints where a virtual light hits the bevel. Selected areas have a luminous dense turquoise glass interior, dark tracks are solid. These are stylized local shading cues achievable analytically in a shader, NOT actual see-through frosted glass or real scene reflections.
Aesthetic quality is critical: premium and materially rich like the reference, NOT wireframe boxes with a triangle pasted in each corner, NOT flat teal rectangles, NOT generic CSS glassmorphism, NOT blurry neon soup. Use real apparent depth at the bevels, multiple subtle layers of specular response and restrained short-range light bloom. Make corner facets asymmetric and light-dependent, with faint internal seams rather than solid opaque polygons. Secondary components have quieter rims than active ones. A dominant light is above-left. No pink except the deliberately small error state.
Composition: flat front-on orthographic component-design reference sheet on uniform almost-black navy background. All component edges horizontal/vertical, no perspective, no floating isometric screens, no environment, no floor, no atmospheric texture. Crisp geometry and legible small condensed mono typography. Thoughtful aligned layout with generous gaps; omit unnecessary fake data or ornaments. Each module is large enough to inspect the material. Tiny family/state labels outside controls. Large high-resolution landscape image. Avoid excessive empty space, heavy grid cell frames, large titles, watermarks, pseudo-technical decoration.
Native GUI usability: preserve legible labels; glow stays tight; focus is a distinct outline with an even gap; selected and disabled states are unmistakable. Beveled paired corner cuts on rectangular bodies, subtly eased joins; true circular geometry on round controls. Colors are roles (primary cyan, secondary blue, cool neutral, occasional restrained amber).

Create a refined reference sheet of SELECTION components in 6 clearly separated modules, each with a few actual related states:
1 segmented switch, three joined segments labelled "Overview", "Activity", "History". Show idle, one cyan selected, and visible keyboard focus variation. A single coherent docked silhouette; internal separators quiet.
2 tab strip labelled "Log", "Progress", "Insights" above a short dark content well. The active tab has a luminous glass lip / underlit edge, not a boxy filled rectangle. Include hovered tab.
3 single dropdown "Bench Press" both closed and open with three options; selected option is a tasteful cyan glass highlight and check, secondary choices quiet.
4 searchable multiselect with search text and two compact removable selected chips, anchored options beneath. Enough detail to establish input, menu, chip and mark materials.
5 radio group with a circular optical-glass ring and a luminous inset selected center, including idle/selected/disabled.
6 small tree/list with parent "Workspace" and rows "Training", "Recovery", "Reports". Expanded chevron, selected row, focused row, disabled row; quiet indentation guides.
Use actual component reference layouts, not a dashboard. Selected-state contrast and smooth continuation across docked segments matter.

Create a refined reference sheet of OVERLAYS in 6 clearly separated modules:
1 a compact open context menu with "Open", "Duplicate", "Rename", separator and amber "Archive". Show one hovered command and one disabled command. Menu chrome is a single substantial glass slab; internal rows are mostly quiet except active row.
2 a small anchored popover headed "Session details" with two label/value pairs and a small close glyph. Visible beveled glass rim, corner refractive facets, opaque quiet interior.
3 a tooltip above its anchor reading "Add a workout"; small, precise, dimensional optical edge, readable, no giant glow.
4 an open confirmation dialog "Save changes?", brief line "Your session will be updated.", secondary "Cancel" and primary "Save" buttons, a close glyph. Showcase layered glass panels and buttons without stacking noisy frames.
5 three compact toast notifications: cyan check "Changes saved", amber "Storage almost full", muted red "Connection lost". Semantic status in small icon/edge cue, not a giant saturated surface.
6 a minimal floating window header with title and minimize/maximize/close controls, showing normal and hovered close glyph.
Consistent reference style; demonstrate differences in elevation through bevel, inset border and local highlight—not backdrop blur. No cropped components.

Create a refined reference sheet of VALUE and FEEDBACK components in 6 modules:
1 a labelled slider "GAIN" with thin opaque dark recessed rail, brilliant dense cyan fill, small substantial beveled glass thumb. Include a dual-thumb range slider and a disabled variant, with sparse readable numeric ticks.
2 a round knob "BALANCE" with genuine concentric glass depth: restrained dark solid dial body, hairline concentric bevels, segmented cyan value arc, fine ticks, tiny luminous pointer, centered "+35". Show normal and focused variants. No square button pretending to be a dial.
3 numeric stepper "EXPOSURE" with "− 1.25 +"; one continuous glass frame, subtle separate hit areas, fine dividers, hovered increment.
4 progress bars including 62%, completed and a segmented capacity meter. The filled regions are luminous SOLID glass with localized pale glints and sharply bounded faint reflection planes, visibly richer than flat cyan paint. Track opaque dark.
5 circular progress at "62%", small spinner, success and error rings. Fine dimensional rims and crisp arcs, not inflated tubes or fuzzy rings.
6 compact status badges "Online", "Offline", "Warning" and an elegant compact color picker with accurate saturation/value square, hue rail, alpha checker rail and glass chrome; exact functional colors remain readable.
Keep the glass surface craft as sophisticated as the attached source. Show selected, focus and disabled examples without making every control bright. No cluttered dashboard.

Create a refined reference sheet of CONTAINERS and DATA surfaces in 5 large modules:
1 a substantial but restrained settings panel with header "Workspace", small window controls and three key/value rows, footer action "Details". Show optical rim thickness, narrow cyan edge, refractive corner shards and faint local reflection bands on mostly opaque midnight glass. Panel frame subtly chamfered, no square neon corner brackets.
2 the same panel minimized as just its header, beside an expanded and collapsed disclosure row "Channel settings" and a disabled row "Locked configuration".
3 a compact data table with headers "NODE", "STATUS", "LOAD", five rows. One row selected with a dense cyan underlit glass strip, one cell keyboard-focused with thin evenly inset outline, one cell as edit field. Body rows are quiet and legible—do NOT put triangular facets and frames around every cell or every row. Material richness belongs to the table enclosure and selected surface.
4 a scrollable list and an adjacent virtualized list "Items"; show dark recessed scroll tracks and solid beveled cyan-glass thumbs with tight highlight. Native proportions, no oversized scrollbars.
5 a small empty panel "No records" plus a quiet inset separator/header/footer detail.
Give the larger panels convincing stylized glass depth through multi-layer edge highlights and asymmetrical corner light response, not wide bevel gradients or transparency. True flat UI reference, all labels readable. No perspective, no decorative HUD widgets.
